snapshot.exam_hook: ⚡ SSC Polity Hook: 35: Age. 72: Pardon. 123: Ordinance. 76: AG. Real head: PM. Nominal head: Pres.

quick_notes.title: The President (Art 52–62)
quick_notes.detail: Nominal Head. First Citizen. Elected by Electoral College (MPs + MLAs). Term : 5 years. Minimum Age : 35.
quick_notes.explanation: The President of India, as described in Articles 52 to 62 of the Constitution, is the nominal head of state, meaning the President is the ceremonial leader who formally performs duties but does not hold real executive power. The President is also the first citizen of India, which is a title of highest honor. The President is elected by an Electoral College composed of elected Members of Parliament (MPs), who are the people's representatives in the national legislature, and elected Members of Legislative Assemblies (MLAs), who are state-level representatives. The President's term lasts for five years, and a candidate must be at least 35 years old to be eligible for the office.

quick_notes.title: Powers of President
quick_notes.detail: Veto power. Pardoning power (Art 72). Ordinance power (Art 123). Appoints PM, Governors, CJI, CAG.
quick_notes.explanation: The President of India has several important powers. The veto power means the President can refuse to sign a bill passed by Parliament, sending it back for reconsideration, or choose to not act on it at all. The pardoning power, under Article 72 of the Constitution, allows the President to forgive or reduce a punishment, including the death penalty, for someone convicted of a crime under central law. The ordinance power, under Article 123, lets the President issue a temporary law with the same force as an Act of Parliament when Parliament is not in session. The President also appoints key officials: the Prime Minister (PM), the Governors of states, the Chief Justice of India (CJI), and the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG), who audits government spending.

quick_notes.title: Prime Minister
quick_notes.detail: Real Head. Appointed by President. Head of Council of Ministers. Term : Pleasure of President (usually 5 years).
quick_notes.explanation: Prime Minister (PM) is the real head of the government in India, meaning the person who actually leads the country's day-to-day administration. The President of India appoints the Prime Minister, usually choosing the leader of the political party that wins the most seats in the Lok Sabha, the lower house of Parliament. The Prime Minister becomes the head of the Council of Ministers, which is the group of senior ministers who assist in running the government. The term of the Prime Minister is at the pleasure of the President, which means the PM can stay in office as long as the President has confidence in them, and this usually lasts until the next general election, around five years.

quick_notes.title: Vice-President (Art 63)
quick_notes.detail: Ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha. Presides over RS. Term : 5 years.
quick_notes.explanation: Vice-President (Article 63) The Vice-President of India is the second-highest constitutional office, and Article 63 of the Constitution creates this post. The Vice-President automatically serves as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, which means that by holding the office of Vice-President, they become the permanent presiding officer of the upper house of Parliament. As Chairman, the Vice-President's main job is to preside over the sessions of the Rajya Sabha, maintaining order and deciding who gets to speak. The term of office for the Vice-President is five years, and they can be re-elected for multiple terms.
